name: Angela Bennett
current_role: Head of Wright Prospecting; principal of AMB Holdings (family investment company), Perth
profile: Australian iron-ore heiress whose wealth comes from Wright Prospecting's share of the Rio Tinto royalty negotiated by her father Peter Wright with Lang Hancock. She took over Wright Prospecting with her brother Michael after their father's 1985 death; in Dec 2025 sold a 15% stake in the Rhodes Ridge project to Mitsui in a ~$2B deal. Son Todd runs AMB Holdings.
interesting_fact: Her wealth stems from a royalty on every tonne of iron ore Rio Tinto mines in parts of Western Australia, negotiated decades ago by her father and Lang Hancock (father of Gina Rinehart).
deep_cut_fact: Ruah's 11-storey Perth shelter for homeless women and children is named the Angela Wright Bennett Centre after her donation; her foundation also gave $250,000 to autism research at the Kids Research Institute in 2015.
notes: Described as reclusive and rarely seen in public; no personal/public channels found. Angela Wright Bennett Foundation (program director David MacKenzie) funds climate/nature work; best route likely via AMB Holdings / foundation. Avoid the Rinehart litigation and family disputes in outreach.

name: Prem Watsa
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Fairfax Financial Holdings (Toronto)
profile: Hyderabad-born, IIT Madras-trained engineer who emigrated to Canada in 1972, earned an MBA at Western's Ivey school, worked at Confederation Life, and in 1985 took control of what became Fairfax Financial, a value-investing insurance and investment holding company often compared to Berkshire Hathaway. He still runs Fairfax, which reported $1.39B Q2 2026 net earnings.
interesting_fact: Often called 'Canada's Warren Buffett', he has led Fairfax since 1985 with a value-investing approach and still delivers the opening remarks at its annual meeting (the 41st was held in April 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He arrived in London, Ontario with just 8 rupees and paid his way through his Ivey MBA by selling air conditioners and furnaces; in 2017 he became Huron University College's first-ever Chancellor.

public_contacts.value: John Varnell, VP Corporate Development, Fairfax Financial (published contact on press releases; phone +1 416-367-4941)

notes: No personal social accounts. Fairfax press releases list John Varnell as the contact (phone only, no email published). Watsa writes a widely read annual shareholder letter, a good hook for outreach.

name: Edward C. (Ned) Johnson
profile: Edward C. 'Ned' Johnson III, longtime chairman and CEO of Fidelity Investments, died on March 23, 2022 at age 91 at his home in Florida.
notes: Deceased March 23, 2022 (source: https://www.cnbc.com/2022/03/24/fidelity-investments-longtime-leader-edward-c-ned-johnson-iii-dies-at-91-.html). Fidelity is now led by his daughter Abigail Johnson; the family wealth is held by his heirs.

name: Howard Schultz
current_role: Lifelong Chairman Emeritus, Starbucks; co-founder, Schultz Family Foundation; investor via Maveron
profile: Brooklyn-raised entrepreneur who joined Starbucks in 1982, founded Il Giornale, then bought and scaled Starbucks from 11 stores to 35,000+ worldwide over three stints as CEO (last ended 2023). He left the board in 2023 as lifelong chairman emeritus, invests in consumer startups through Maveron, and funds veteran and youth job programs via the Schultz Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: He grew up in a Brooklyn housing project and was the first in his family to graduate from college, attending Northern Michigan University on a football scholarship.
deep_cut_fact: Before Starbucks he sold Xerox machines in New York, then ran US operations for Swedish housewares maker Hammarplast; noticing a small Seattle shop ordering unusually many drip coffeemakers led him to visit Starbucks in 1981.
notes: Reported in 2026 to have moved from Washington state to Florida for a 'retirement phase' (verify). He posts occasionally on LinkedIn. Foundation site blocks automated fetches, so no foundation email was verified.

name: Warren Stephens
current_role: 68th U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom (since May 2025); chairman of family investment bank Stephens Inc. (Little Rock)
profile: Son of Jackson Stephens, he grew up in Little Rock's Stephens Inc. (founded by his uncle Witt in 1933, underwriter of Walmart's 1970 IPO), became CEO in 1986 and bought out his cousins in 2006. He stepped back as CEO in January 2025, with his sons named co-CEOs, to serve as Trump's ambassador in London.
interesting_fact: A golf nut, he built the Tom Fazio-designed Alotian Club overlooking Lake Maumelle, Arkansas (opened 2004), ranked #37 in Golf Digest's 2025 list of America's greatest courses.
deep_cut_fact: He contributed land and financing for Dickey-Stephens Park, the North Little Rock minor-league ballpark opened in 2007 that is named jointly for the Stephens brothers and baseball's Dickey brothers (Yankees Hall of Famer Bill Dickey).

public_contacts.value: https://uk.usembassy.gov/ (U.S. Embassy London, his official office)

notes: As a serving ambassador, podcast requests would go through the U.S. Embassy London press office; he is unlikely to discuss business while in post. Washington and Lee BA (1979), Wake Forest MBA (1981).

name: Matteo Danieli
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons (Milan); has served as VP of Product / former Chief Product Officer
profile: Italian engineer who co-founded Bending Spoons in 2013 with Luca Ferrari, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella after their note-taking startup Evertale failed. Largely bootstrapped until 2022, Bending Spoons buys apps with loyal users and overhauls them (Evernote, Meetup, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and was valued at ~$11B in October 2025, Italy's most valuable startup.
interesting_fact: The four cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen; their first venture, Evertale, failed before they relaunched as Bending Spoons and later moved to Milan.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1984, he graduated with honours in Information Engineering from the University of Padua through the T.I.M.E. double-degree programme with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), where the Copenhagen connection began; he was Evertale's CTO.
notes: Lower-profile than CEO Luca Ferrari. Reportedly stepped down from the CPO role because he felt someone else could add more value, in line with the company's meritocracy culture (per a Sourcery interview summary, unverified). Has appeared on podcasts, so he may be open to one.

name: Richard Chandler
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Clermont Group (Singapore); founder, Chandler Foundation
profile: New Zealand-born investor who began investing in 1982, built Sovereign Global with his brother Christopher (a deep-value, emerging-markets investor), split assets in 2006 and founded Singapore-based Clermont Group. Clermont holds healthcare, financial services and aerospace assets, including India's SBFC, Vietnam's Hoan My hospitals and electric-aviation firm magniX; he also funds good-governance work.
interesting_fact: Clermont owns magniX, maker of electric powertrains and energy storage for aircraft, which won a $74M five-year NASA contract in 2021 for electrified aircraft propulsion research.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Matangi, New Zealand, the son of a beekeeper, he went on to found the Chandler Institute of Governance in Singapore (2019), which publishes the annual Chandler Good Government Index ranking 100+ countries.
notes: Private; no published email found. magniX (electric aviation) gives a natural energy-angle hook. Background sourced from Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Chandler_(businessman)

name: Rafique Abdul Malik
profile: Indian footwear retailer who turned the single Colaba, Mumbai shoe store his father Malik Tejani acquired in 1955 into Metro Brands, one of India's largest and most profitable footwear chains (~800 stores) with Metro Shoes, Mochi and Walkway plus franchises for Crocs, FitFlop, Fila and Foot Locker. Metro Brands is listed; daughter Farah Malik Bhanji is MD and Nissan Joseph CEO.
interesting_fact: Metro started as one standalone shoe shop in Colaba, Mumbai, and over three generations grew into a 'Made in India' footwear house of brands with roughly 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: He has been chairman since 19 January 1977, the month Metro Shoes was incorporated, giving him nearly five decades at the helm; the company bio also notes he is a Harvard alumnus.
notes: Low public profile; daughter and MD Farah Malik Bhanji is the usual public face. The company site has a Media section that may list a PR contact.

name: Harindarpal Banga
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, The Caravel Group (Hong Kong); son Angad became Group CEO in January 2026
profile: Chandigarh-raised master mariner who moved to Hong Kong in 1979, became an early partner and later vice-chairman at commodity trader Noble Group over a 21-year career, then sold out by 2012 and founded The Caravel Group in 2013, which trades commodities and runs shipping. An early investor in Nykaa, he handed the CEO role to son Angad in 2026 and now focuses on strategy and governance.
interesting_fact: He was an early investor in Indian beauty e-retailer Nykaa and still holds a stake after its 2021 Mumbai IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before trading commodities he was a seafarer: trained on the Training Ship Dufferin, India's oldest maritime academy, he earned his Master Mariner certificate in 1976 and was commanding merchant vessels at 27.
notes: Caravel issues releases via PR Newswire; no published email found on the site (JS-rendered). Philanthropy runs through The Caravel Foundation. Received India's Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2011.

name: Christina Rohde
current_role: Largest shareholder, Rohde & Schwarz (Munich); no confirmed operating role
profile: Heir from the Rohde founding family and the largest shareholder of Rohde & Schwarz, the Munich test-and-measurement, broadcast, secure communications and defence-electronics group founded in 1933 by physicists Lothar Rohde and Hermann Schwarz. The company, with over 3 billion euros in revenue, is still controlled by both founding families and has paid more than 2.3 billion euros in dividends since 2006.
interesting_fact: Rohde & Schwarz was founded in summer 1933 as a lab in a Munich apartment at Thierschstrasse 36; its first product was a portable crystal clock.
notes: Extremely private; no public biography, interviews or confirmed personal details found, so alive status and exact relationship to Lothar Rohde are unverified. Web search budget ran out during this lane, so research was limited. Only company channels exist.

name: Jimmy John Liautaud
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Jimmy John's (now part of Inspire Brands); private investor
profile: Illinois entrepreneur who opened Jimmy John's in 1983 at 19 with a $25,000 loan from his father, an Army veteran, and grew it into a ~2,800-unit, almost entirely franchised sandwich chain. He sold a majority stake to Roark Capital in 2016 and merged his remaining stake into Roark's Inspire Brands in 2019.
interesting_fact: His father's $25,000 loan came with a condition: if the sandwich business failed, Jimmy John would enlist in the US Army; in exchange his father took a 48% stake.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he gave $1 million to his old high school, Elgin Academy, on condition the building also bear the name of James Lyons, the dean who disciplined him there; the upper school is now the Liautaud-Lyons Upper School.
notes: No published personal or office contact found; Jimmy John's media now handled by Inspire Brands. He also co-funded (with his father) the Liautaud Graduate School of Business at UIC with a $5M gift. Avoid big-game-hunting controversy in outreach.

name: Zhou Zhiwen
current_role: Major shareholder of JOINN Laboratories (Beijing; SSE 603127 / HKEX 6127); current board title not verified
profile: Listed as a billionaire through his stake in JOINN Laboratories (昭衍新药), a Beijing contract research organization founded in 1995 that provides non-clinical safety/toxicology studies, clinical trial and pharmacovigilance services, and lab animal models, with facilities in Beijing, Suzhou, Guangzhou, San Francisco and Boston. It is dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: JOINN, founded in Beijing in 1995, has passed China NMPA GLP certification ten times and runs research sites in San Francisco (since 2013) and Boston (since 2019), as well as across China.

public_contacts.value: jiafengsong@joinn-lab.com (JOINN investor relations contact Jia Fengsong; tel 010-67869582)

notes: Could not verify his biography or current role (web search budget exhausted mid-lane; no Wikipedia article). He is widely reported as co-founder alongside chair Feng Yuxia, but this was not verified here; check HKEX annual-report director bios before outreach. Media cooperation line on site: 010-67869966-1811.

name: Bris Rocher
current_role: Chairman, Groupe Rocher (La Gacilly / Issy-les-Moulineaux, France)
profile: Grandson of Yves Rocher, he joined the family company at 16 without finishing his baccalaureate, trained at Arthur Andersen in the US, and became CEO at 31 after his grandfather's death in 2009. He bought back Sanofi's 19.3% stake in 2012, acquired US-based Arbonne in 2018, and in 2023 handed the CEO role to Jean-David Schwartz while staying chairman of the family-controlled group (Yves Rocher, Arbonne, Sabon, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Petit Bateau).
interesting_fact: He joined Yves Rocher at 16 without a baccalaureate after his father Didier died; his grandfather groomed him as successor and he became CEO at 31.
deep_cut_fact: As a young man he wanted to become a jazz guitarist before joining the family business.
notes: Groupe Rocher markets itself as a 'mission-driven company' (entreprise a mission) focused on reconnecting people with nature, a good angle for sustainability-themed outreach. The site has a Press section but no press email found in static HTML.

name: Joe Lacob
current_role: Co-executive chairman and CEO, Golden State Warriors; principal owner, Golden State Valkyries (WNBA)
profile: New Bedford, Massachusetts native and former Kleiner Perkins partner (from 1987, 50+ startup investments) who led the group that bought the Golden State Warriors for $450M in 2010. The team has since won four NBA titles, opened the privately financed Chase Center, and launched the WNBA expansion Golden State Valkyries (record $50M fee), which have sold out home games and made the playoffs.
interesting_fact: The Warriors went 73-9 in 2015-16, the best regular-season record in NBA history, and have won four titles under his ownership; the team's value has risen roughly 15-fold since he bought it.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he trained in public health, earning a master's in epidemiology at UCLA; and in the 1990s he was a primary investor in the American Basketball League, an early women's pro league, decades before launching the Valkyries.

public_contacts.value: https://www.nba.com/warriors (Golden State Warriors; media relations via team)

notes: Best route is the Warriors' communications/media relations department. VC background (Kleiner Perkins, energy/cleantech-era investments) could be a natural podcast hook. Avoid mentioning his late wife.

name: Matthew Roszak
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Bloq (Chicago blockchain infrastructure company)
profile: Chicago-based venture capitalist (Lake Forest College, 1995) who worked in VC and as an entrepreneur in the 1990s-2000s, began building a crypto portfolio in 2012, and co-founded Bloq, which provides blockchain infrastructure, digital-asset custody consulting for banks and stablecoin transaction services.
interesting_fact: He co-led an initiative to give every member of the US Congress $50 worth of digital assets so lawmakers could experience crypto firsthand; some accepted.
notes: Bloq's website blocked automated access and web search budget ran out, so no verified contact or deep-cut fact. Bloq's own site or press page is the likely route. Avoid the 2006 SEC settlement (Blue Rhino) in outreach. Bloq's crypto/Bitcoin mining-adjacent infrastructure could tie into energy/data-center themes.

name: Jerry Moyes
current_role: Owner, SME Industries (steel fabrication and construction, Utah); founder and former chairman/CEO of Swift Transportation
profile: Born in 1944, he and his father founded Swift Transportation in 1966 with one truck hauling cotton and imported steel between Arizona and California, building it to nearly 20,000 trucks and ~$4B revenue before its 2017 merger with Knight Transportation. Having sold much of his Knight-Swift stake, he now concentrates on SME Industries, a Utah steel fabricator and construction company.
interesting_fact: Swift began in 1966 with a single truck moving cotton and imported steel between Arizona and California and grew into one of America's largest trucking fleets.
deep_cut_fact: He is a graduate of Weber State College in Ogden, Utah (Goddard School of Business & Economics) and once served as president of the Arizona Motor Transport Association; he also owned the charter airline Swift Air.
notes: No published personal/office contact found; SME Industries is the likely route. Alive status inferred (no death reported on Wikipedia), not freshly confirmed because search budget ran out. Avoid the insider-trading case, Coyotes bankruptcy and iAero bankruptcy in outreach.

name: Shari Arison Dorsman
current_role: Owner, Arison Group / Arison Investments and The Ted Arison Family Foundation (Israel)
profile: New York-born Israeli businesswoman and philanthropist (b. 1957), daughter of Carnival Cruise Lines founder Ted Arison and sister of Micky Arison. Her inherited Carnival wealth was invested through Arison Investments, including long-time controlling stakes in Bank Hapoalim and Shikun & Binui; today the Arison Group focuses on impact investing and philanthropy under her 'Doing Good Model'.
interesting_fact: She initiated Good Deeds Day in 2007 with 7,000 volunteers in Israel; it has since grown into a global day of volunteering involving millions of people in many countries.
deep_cut_fact: Her personal motto, quoted on Good Deeds Day's site: 'if people will think good, speak good and do good, the circles of goodness will grow in the world.' She also founded Goodnet.org, a publication devoted entirely to good-news stories, and has written books on spirituality and business.
notes: Forbes lists her as 'Shari Arison Dorsman'; she is publicly known as Shari Arison. Her official site has a contact page and links to Facebook (ShariArisonOfficial) and Instagram. Avoid Bank Hapoalim layoffs and divorces in outreach. Born 9 Sept 1957 (Wikipedia).

name: Bryan Glazer
current_role: Co-chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (with brothers Joel and Edward); director, Manchester United
profile: Son of shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), he and his five siblings own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers (bought for $192M in 1995, now worth ~$5.2B) and a controlling stake in Manchester United (bought 2005; a quarter of their stake sold to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023). He has helped run the Bucs since 1995, including the new stadium and brand redesign, and the team has won Super Bowls XXXVII and LV.
interesting_fact: Under Glazer ownership the Buccaneers won Super Bowl LV (2021), the first time a team played the Super Bowl in its own home stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He majored in broadcast communications at American University before earning a law degree at Whittier; in 2016 he gave $4M to convert Tampa's historic Fort Homer W. Hesterly Armory into the Bryan Glazer Family Jewish Community Center.

public_contacts.value: https://www.buccaneers.com/ (Tampa Bay Buccaneers; route via team communications)

notes: The Glazers rarely give interviews, especially about Manchester United, so avoid United fan-protest topics. Best route is the Buccaneers communications department. He was a key figure in the design of Raymond James Stadium and the Bucs' logo redesign.

name: Rosely Schweizer
current_role: Shareholder (~12.5%) of Dr. August Oetker KG; former advisory board chair (until 2010)
profile: Born Rosely Oetker in Hamburg in 1940, eldest daughter of Rudolf-August Oetker, she studied economics in Innsbruck (1964), was a general partner and advisory board chair at sparkling-wine maker Henkell & Soehnlein, and chaired the Oetker parent company's advisory board from 2007 to 2010. She owns about 12.5% of the food, beverage and hotel group; her son Rudolf Louis Schweizer became board chairman in 2019.
interesting_fact: In 2001 she co-founded, with the German association of women entrepreneurs, the Kaete-Ahlmann-Foundation, named after her grandmother, to support female entrepreneurs.
deep_cut_fact: Besides business she had a long political career: Murrhardt town councillor 1984-2006 and CDU member of the Baden-Wuerttemberg state parliament 1992-2001 for the Backnang constituency, where she was the party's economic-policy spokesperson.
notes: Aged ~86; no death reported on German Wikipedia (alive status not freshly confirmed). Lives in Murrhardt area; very private. Holds the Bundesverdienstkreuz (Federal Cross of Merit). Avoid her father's wartime past in outreach.

name: Robert P Stiller
current_role: Private investor; founder and former president/CEO of Green Mountain Coffee Roasters (now part of Keurig Dr Pepper)
profile: Entrepreneur who co-founded rolling-paper maker E-Z Wider in 1972, then in 1981 bought into a tiny Vermont roaster, Green Mountain Coffee, becoming sole owner about a year later. He took it public in 1993, invested early in single-serve brewer Keurig, ran it as CEO until 2007, and the business became Keurig Green Mountain and later part of Keurig Dr Pepper, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: In 2001 he was named Forbes's first-ever 'Entrepreneur of the Year'; Green Mountain made its first investment in Keurig in 1993, the year of its IPO.
deep_cut_fact: He found Green Mountain Coffee by tasting it at a Vermont ski resort in 1981 and bought a two-thirds stake in the Waitsfield roaster with a partner, a decade after co-founding E-Z Wider rolling papers.
notes: Very low public profile in recent years; no published personal, office or foundation contact found (web search budget ran out). Journalist Michael Gross profiled him as 'EZ Wider Maker, Green Mountain Coffee Roaster, Spiritual Seeker': https://www.mgross.com/books/my-generation/my-generation-bonus-chapters/bob-stiller-ez-wider-maker-green-mountain-coffee-roaster-spiritual-seeker/ . New York Military Academy class of '61.
